unresolved_added: Insurance alpha is explicitly arbitrary, w is equated to an unspecified fair value, and no market, loss, demand, or percent-convention calibration supports the premium-revenue equation.
The generic removal-cost sum multiplies p_t by q_t although p_t is alternately a catcher price or conduct cost and q_t is alternately debris capacity or conduct count; units and indexing conflict.

The compensation formula multiplies by epsilon even though the notation table defines epsilon as debris removed per space trapper; n_(t-1) is also not reconciled with exposure from surviving satellites.
The Cobb-Douglas construction sets x2=alpha*w and k=0.5 without economic estimation, leaves mu unidentified, and converts utility into compensation without a dimensional or actuarial justification.
The symbol alpha is reused for the insurance rate and Gamma shape, while Gamma parameters, fitted observations, ring boundaries, normalization, and goodness of fit are absent.
Visual resemblance between a cited NASA curve and one Gamma-family curve is not parameter estimation or evidence that a two-dimensional radial law represents the selected 1-10 cm debris population.
The approximately fifteen-percent binary occupancy is admitted to be an educated guess; the area-to-count explanation has no units, debris count, valid-cell denominator, or reproducible calculation.
Same-cell collision probability depends on the arbitrary 1000 by 1000 grid, cell-to-altitude mapping, occupancy rules, satellite footprint, and time step, none of which receive a resolution study.

The printed debris update is self-referential Q_t=Q_t-(...) rather than a transition from Q_(t-1), and it omits the growth term described immediately afterward; it is retained verbatim rather than silently repaired.

The source calls its baseline debris trend linear but implements or discusses a five-percent annual increase; no complete linear, geometric, or logarithmic recurrence and no fitted parameters are supplied.
Random removal and growth omit coordinate-to-altitude conversion, accessible-cell selection, overflow and boundary handling, random seeds, repetition counts, and a mass-balance diagnostic.
The launch recurrence n_1=110 and n_t=1.05*n_(t-1) is reconstructed from prose; the plotted 2001-2015 series is not fitted to justify either 110 or five percent.

The law-of-large-numbers statement has no independent-run protocol, sample size, seed ledger, convergence plot, Monte Carlo error, confidence interval, or check that the simulated trials match the claimed probability.
The land equation adds initial cost C0 to C_1t without a one-time indicator, so the printed form can charge the initial investment every year rather than only at project start.
The land, space, and combined paths rely on unreported prices, removal counts, insured values, commission, compensation scale, growth arrays, seeds, MATLAB code, and raw yearly outputs.

The near-16-billion combined result is a single undiscounted scenario with no currency year, financing constraint, opportunity cost, demand response, joint uncertainty, or external commercial validation.
The paper reports 8,004-6,374 as 1,670, but the arithmetic difference is 1,630; the printed sensitivity sequence must preserve this source error and use 1,630 in any corrected analysis.
The logarithmic-growth scenario reports an ending count of 5,313 without an equation, fitted historical data, parameters, time origin, or comparable scenario likelihood.

Rocket lifetimes of 3, 6, 9, and 12 form a four-point one-factor sweep; launch cadence, refurbishment cost, failure risk, capacity, replacement rule, and derivation of 0.38 billion per additional use are absent.

The alpha=3 percent prose says the firm enjoys net income in the first nine years, while Figure 24 is negative for roughly those years; the visual supports an early-loss, not early-income, interpretation.

Alpha changes both premium revenue and the constructed compensation amount, but the sensitivity narrative treats it mainly as revenue and ignores insurance demand, competition, claims frequency, percent conventions, and joint parameter changes.

Best-response inspection confirms the stated baseline and policy pure equilibria, but payoff derivation, units, probability weighting, strategy costs, policy implementation cost, and external validity are not supplied.

The Pareto-improvement claim is supportable only inside the two printed matrices; it omits policymakers, third parties, orbital externalities, enforcement, mixed strategies, uncertainty, and welfare aggregation.

Claims of robust profit, accurate graphs, thorough sensitivity, optimal removal, and necessary standards exceed the uncalibrated field, arbitrary parameters, local sweeps, missing code, undiscounted accounting, and absent joint or out-of-sample validation.
